system.description: This species is a new one to many marine biologists, as they are quite adept at hiding in plain sight. However, due to some strange circumstances, gorging sharks ( Cetorhinus gigantus ) seem to find the waters three hundred kilometers off Land's End to OCEANS, SEAS, AND LAKES // be rather fascinating, as well as the coast along the Norfolk Stinkfens. Both of these locations are very popular for gorging sharks, and their mundane progenitors the basking shark ( Cetorhinus maximus ), to gather in shoals and schools as they go through their summer courtship behaviors (yes, these are the sharks that swim nose to tail in circles for hours at a time). Before the Awakening, the basking shark was the second largest species of shark, behind the whale shark. After the Awakening, the megalodon became the largest species of shark … until recently. The gorging shark is, as far as modern science is aware, the largest species of shark in the world. The largest specimen ever recorded, a male over twenty-three meters in length, was recovered after it was killed by unknown parties off the Norfolk coast in 2078.
